title: Hypertension Management Guidance
recommendation_blocks: Target BP <140/90 mmHg for most adults.
Target BP <130/80 mmHg when diabetes or chronic kidney disease is present.
Start lifestyle measures alongside pharmacologic therapy when persistent elevation exists.
Use ACE inhibitor or ARB as first-line treatment unless contraindicated.

contraindications.label: pregnancy
contraindications.reason: Avoid ACE inhibitors and ARBs in pregnancy; use pregnancy-safe alternatives.

contraindications.label: hyperkalemia
contraindications.reason: RAAS blockers can worsen hyperkalemia; review potassium before initiating.

title: Type 2 Diabetes Management Guidance
recommendation_blocks: Target HbA1c <7% for most adults unless individualized goals are required.
Use metformin first-line unless renal function or intolerance prevents it.
Prefer SGLT2 inhibitor or GLP-1 agonist when ASCVD, heart failure, or CKD is present.
Review HbA1c every 3 to 6 months and maintain annual eye and foot checks.

contraindications.label: renal_impairment
contraindications.reason: Metformin use becomes unsafe with severe renal impairment; confirm eGFR before initiation.

title: Adult Community-Acquired Pneumonia Guidance
recommendation_blocks: Use a severity tool such as CURB-65 or PSI to guide disposition.
For inpatient empirical therapy, consider ceftriaxone plus azithromycin when appropriate.
Reassess response within 48 to 72 hours and narrow therapy when cultures or trajectory allow.

contraindications.label: penicillin_allergy
contraindications.reason: Avoid beta-lactam empirical choices when severe beta-lactam allergy exists.

medication_warnings.message: Monitor INR closely because common pneumonia antibiotics can interact with warfarin.

title: Urinary Tract Infection Guidance
recommendation_blocks: Treat uncomplicated cystitis with a short-course first-line antibiotic when culture and local resistance patterns allow.
Use broader or parenteral coverage for pyelonephritis or systemic features.

contraindications.label: pregnancy
contraindications.reason: Avoid trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and fluoroquinolones in pregnancy when alternatives are available.
